name: Ice Cream Shop Revenue
description: Size the annual revenue of a single ice cream shop location.
formula: Revenue = Annual foot traffic x % who notice x % who buy x cones per purchase x price per cone
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify noticing traffic = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply purchase rate = noticing_traffic x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate spend per purchase = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate annual revenue = buyers x spend_per_purchase
key_insight: There's no population or citywide market to narrow down here -- this is a single-location estimate, built up from foot traffic past this one spot, not down from a city's population.
common_mistakes: Trying to size the citywide ice cream market instead of this one shop's foot traffic
Skipping the "who notices" filter and assuming everyone who walks by is a potential customer
Forgetting cones-per-purchase and pricing off a single scoop instead of the average purchase
framework_soundbite: One location, foot traffic in, conversion twice, price out -- there's no population to narrow down from.
business_contexts: a single-location ice cream shop owner planning next year's budget
a franchise evaluating a new storefront's revenue potential
question_patterns: A franchise is evaluating whether a candidate storefront can support an ice cream shop and wants a bottom-up revenue estimate before signing the lease.

target_population.unit: people/year (annual foot traffic near the shop)

display_context: Food & Beverage • Ice Cream Shop Sizing

prompts.beginner: Estimate the annual revenue of a single ice cream shop on a busy street corner.
prompts.intermediate: A franchise is evaluating whether a candidate storefront can support an ice cream shop and wants a bottom-up revenue estimate before signing the lease.
prompts.advanced: An ice cream franchise's real estate team has three candidate storefronts and limited capital to open only one this year. Before committing, they want a defensible bottom-up revenue estimate for the strongest candidate -- built from foot traffic, not a citywide estimate.

approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Start from the foot traffic actually near this one shop, filter down to who notices and who buys, then multiply by what they spend -- you're building the whole estimate up from this single location, since there's no larger market to narrow down from.
